About Simulation

A robot bin for crowded events

s'aat

A trash bin that comes to you.

s'aat drives around busy places like markets, concerts and stadiums. It picks up the litter people drop. When someone walks past holding trash, it opens its lid and smiles at them.

The problem

There are never enough bins where people are.

Think of Chatuchak at closing time, or the field after Big Mountain. People are tired, their hands are full, and the nearest bin is far away. So a lot of it ends up on the ground.

The bins are in the wrong place

Most bins sit at the edge of the venue. People eat and drink in the middle, so that's where the trash ends up.

Cleaning only starts at the end

Cleaners come in once everyone has gone home. By then plastic has blown into the drains and food is stuck to the ground.

Nobody gets a reason to change

Putting trash in a bin feels the same as dropping it. Nothing reacts, so people do the same thing at the next event.

How we measure it

We track two numbers.

How much trash goes into a bin, and how much litter is left on the ground. The simulation shows both, without and with s'aat.

      Why today's fixes fall short

      Three tools, three gaps.

      Fixed bins

      Stand at the edges. Litter piles up in the middle, where people actually are.

      Too far away
      Cleanup crews

      Arrive after the crowd leaves, when waste is trodden in or washed into drains.

      Too late
      Campaigns and signs

      Ask people to do the right thing, but nothing responds when they do.

      No feedback

      Flip each gap around.

      The bin waits at the edge→The bin comes to you
      Clean after everyone leaves→Clean while people are still there
      A sign asks nicely→A face that smiles back

      3D model needs a connection to load.

      Introducing

      Meet s'aat.

      • Scanning eyesFind litter, people holding trash, and belongings to leave alone
      • All-terrain legsRoll on flat ground, climb curbs and stadium steps
      • Grappling armsPick up bottles, cups and wrappers from the ground
      • Autonomous lidOpens by itself when someone comes close with trash
      • Face displaySmiles when trash goes in, frowns when someone litters
